messages.content: You map test-fixture records to the placeholders of an LLM prompt template, reproducing exactly what the application code does before it formats the prompt. Reply with JSON only.

## Application code (shop/summarize.py; the LLM call is in `summarize`, lines [10, 16])
```python
"""Summarise a ticket thread for handoff."""

SUMMARY_PROMPT = """Write a handoff note for the next support agent in at most 60 words:
Issue, Tried so far, Next step."""


def summarize(client, messages: list[dict]):
    transcript = "\n".join(f"{m['role']}: {m['text']}" for m in messages)
    return client.messages.create(
        model="claude-haiku-4-5",
        max_tokens=200,
        system=SUMMARY_PROMPT,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Thread, {len(messages)} messages:\n\n{transcript}"}],
    )

```

## Prompt template (str.format placeholders)
System: "Write a handoff note for the next support agent in at most 60 words:\nIssue, Tried so far, Next step."
User: "Thread, {len_messages} messages:\n\n{transcript}"
Placeholders: ["len_messages", "transcript"]

## Fixture sets in tests/fixtures/
### threads.json (3 records)
First record: {"id": "th-1", "tags": ["short", "en"], "messages": [{"role": "customer", "text": "Charged twice for order SH-3021 (24.50 EUR)."}, {"role": "agent", "text": "I see both charges and will refund one today."}]}

## Task
Pick the one fixture set whose records are the inputs of `summarize` (null if none is), and for EVERY
placeholder give a recipe that computes its value from one record, exactly as the code above does:
- op "value": str(record[field])
- op "len": str(len(record[field]))
- op "join": sep.join(item.format(**element) for element in record[field]), or `empty` when the list is empty
  (mirror the code's join separator, per-element f-string and any `or "..."` fallback).
`item`, `sep` and `empty` are the contents of the Python string literals in the code, escapes included (write
the two characters \n where the code has \n). In `item` the placeholders are the element's keys: write
{sent_at}, not {m.sent_at} or {m['sent_at']}.
`field` is a top-level key of the record; never use a key whose name starts with "expected" (those are
expected outputs, not inputs).
Reply {"fixture": ..., "recipes": [{"var", "field", "op", "item", "sep", "empty"}]}.
